wi_area_82.blurb: A small bouldering spot in the woods of northern Wisconsin, a short drive from Northland College and tucked in beside the Old Grade Road boulders. Three outcrops, each about a hundred feet long and varying in height, run roughly north to south. Around sixteen problems are recorded, mostly V2 to V3 with a few very easy ones and a single V4. The rock was only recently cleared of debris, so expect rough ground between the blocks and plenty of room for new lines. The walk in takes five to ten minutes, a bit longer than at neighbouring Boulder 81.

wi_06_hell_wall_aka_quarry_wall.blurb: A west-facing sandstone wall on the Petenwell ridge near Necedah, and the tallest point along that stretch, so it stands out from the road. Sixteen routes are recorded: nine bolted sport lines, six trad climbs and one top-rope, spanning 5.6 to 5.12 with most in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The right side is steep and roofed with good stone and holds the harder bolted lines. The left side is slabbier, taller and quieter, and reaching it involves a fourth-class scramble down from a ledge. Views are good, and it makes a decent add-on to the busier Y-Crack area.

wi_5_1_ramsay_s_pinnacle.blurb: A small cluster of shorter climbs in the Potholes section of Devil's Lake's East Bluff, west of the Doorway Rocks and reached from the Devil's Doorway Trail. About sixteen routes are recorded, mostly trad with a handful of top-rope lines, running from easy fifth-class terrain up to around 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.7 to 5.9 range. It is a modest, uncrowded corner that suits a short session of moderate leads or top-ropes rather than a full day. Mostly trad gear and a top-rope setup will cover it.

wi_miner_s_boulders_the.blurb: A scattering of fallen blocks and small exposed faces below Grandad Bluff in La Crosse, lying south of The Point. Sixteen problems are recorded, all bouldering, spread widely across the scale: a few V0 to V2 problems, a middle group at V3 to V5, and some hard lines up to V7 for strong climbers. The place has a loose, explore-as-you-go feel rather than a tidy circuit, and it offers a quiet alternative to the bolted sport routes elsewhere on the bluff. Pads are a good idea, and staying on the established trails keeps the slope intact.

wi_2_welcome_to_the_lake.blurb: An easy warm-up circuit of boulders on the lower tier of the North Shore at Devil's Lake. Sixteen problems are recorded, and most are very easy: nine at V0, a few at V1 or below, one V2 and a single V4. The problems tend to be tall, with flat landings underneath, so spotters and pads are useful even on the gentler lines. It is a good first stop for beginners or a place to loosen up before moving to harder blocks nearby, and it sits close to the parking, which keeps the day simple.
wi_2_welcome_to_the_lake.parking_note: Drive past the North Shore ranger station and over the railroad tracks, then turn right and follow the road to the third parking lot.
wi_2_welcome_to_the_lake.approach: From the middle of the lot, walk straight through the tree line and bear left; the boulders sit on the lower tier in the middle of the North Shore.

wi_4_monolith_ridge_west_side.blurb: A bouldering area on the lake side of Monolith Ridge, on the East Bluff of Devil's Lake. Sixteen problems are recorded, running from a very easy V0 up through several V2 to V4 problems and then a hard top end that reaches V9, so there is something for strong boulderers as well as moderate climbers. The Monolith area as a whole is known for a good variety of problems and mostly flat landings. The problems sit on either side of the trail where it dips, so there is little walking between them once you arrive.
wi_4_monolith_ridge_west_side.approach: From the North Shore, follow the East Bluff Trail for roughly half a mile, passing Elephant Rocks and several overlooks. Where the trail dips slightly, the problems lie on both sides of it.

ar_3_shotgun_alley.blurb: A sport crag on the south side of Fitzgerald Mountain near Fayetteville, sitting just to the right of the Swing Station wall. Fifteen bolted routes offer technical, moderate climbing on mostly vertical sandstone, with a few steeper roof moves thrown in. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, and about half of the lines are 5.9, making it a friendly place for climbers working on their lead grade. Rock quality ranges from fair to excellent and some holds are still loosening, so wear a helmet and carry a stick clip.
ar_3_shotgun_alley.parking_note: Leave the car in the Bayyari Park lot.
ar_3_shotgun_alley.approach: From the Bayyari Park lot, head east on the Stage Coach Trail loop, then follow the signed climbers' trail south along the base of the bluff until you meet the cliff.
